source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 5: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions and scope: launcher, world size, backend/version, transport, network interfaces, scheduler, container permissions, GPU topology, and failure timing are unspecified; do not infer platform facts. This is scenario variant 5.

Diagnosis and safe containment:
1. Record job ID, host, rank/local-rank/world-size, PID, timestamps, backend and versions, environment, stderr, and the last initialization stage. Verify each expected rank starts once, sees the same rendezvous/store endpoint, reaches matching barriers in the same order, and remains alive. Check GPU visibility and rank-to-device mapping, driver/runtime compatibility, peer access, topology, clocks, container device permissions, and resource limits.
2. Hypothesis: a rank-specific rendezvous or transport-path failure prevents all ranks from entering the same collective, rather than the collective algorithm itself being defective. Falsify it if all ranks reach the same barrier and a minimal same-node all-reduce succeeds while the full-world case hangs, or if a hang follows tensor size/algorithm with rendezvous and interface checks passing.
3. Run a controlled, randomized blocked matrix with identical software and allocated hosts: single-node and reduced-world versus full-world; minimal all-reduce versus the real initialization; verified interface selections; and bounded initialization timeouts. Repeat enough times to estimate hang, timeout, and success rates, preserving per-rank logs, store reachability, selected interface, topology, GPU mapping, and exact command/config. Change one factor per comparison and do not treat a timeout as proof of root cause.
4. Treat environment/network selection, firewall/port reachability, DNS, mismatched rank membership, topology/visibility, driver or NCCL/PyTorch compatibility, and resource exhaustion as confounders. Compare observed logs and timestamps, not inferred causes.
5. Mitigate conservatively: stop admitting new work, use a bounded watchdog and explicit cleanup, and roll back any interface, topology, timeout, or backend change if correctness, collective completion, error rate, or latency SLOs regress. Canary a reduced scope before full-world rollout; never silently proceed after a partial initialization.

Measurement plan and limits: report counts and rates with denominators for initialization success, timeout, hang, rank failure, and cleanup failure, plus time-to-init and all-reduce correctness checks. Evidence required includes synchronized per-rank traces, rendezvous/store and interface diagnostics, topology/GPU visibility output, minimal all-reduce results, and matched single-node/reduced-world/full-world trials. Without those measurements, confidence is limited and this remains provisional.
risks: root cause may be misattributed without synchronized rank-level evidence
timeouts can mask a slow or dead rank
configuration changes can trade startup success for correctness or SLO regressions
evidence_required: per-rank synchronized logs and initialization stage timestamps
rendezvous/store reachability and selected-interface diagnostics
GPU visibility, rank mapping, topology, versions, and container/resource-limit evidence
controlled single-node/reduced-world/full-world minimal all-reduce results with denominators

Evidence required includes synchronized per-rank traces, rendezvous/store and interface diagnostics, topology/GPU visibility output, minimal all-reduce results, and matched single-node/reduced-world/full-world trials. Without those measurements, confidence is limited and this remains provisional.
risks: root cause may be misattributed without synchronized rank-level evidence
timeouts can mask a slow or dead rank
configuration changes can trade startup success for correctness or SLO regressions
evidence_required: per-rank synchronized logs and initialization stage timestamps
rendezvous/store reachability and selected-interface diagnostics
GPU visibility, rank mapping, topology, versions, and container/resource-limit evidence
controlled single-node/reduced-world/full-world minimal all-reduce results with denominators
